text:
maya: Heads-up — two customers hit 429s during a short burst this morning even though batch metering later showed they were under quota. looks like enforcement is ahead of the pipeline (meter -> enforcement lag).

tom: Ugh. Any idea if this was per-org or per-key enforcement?

maya: Per-key. Bursty traffic from a single API key. The metering pipeline has ~30s ingestion lag right now; enforcer uses the real-time counters that are updated by the aggregator + heartbeat.

jules: Are we sure the heartbeat wasn't missed? we saw a flaky redis connection in the infra logs around that time.

maya: Checked infra logs: aggregator was writing to redis, but the batch write to bigtable was delayed. enforcer uses Redis for fast counters but we do reconciliation periodically from the pipeline. The problem: redis had a stale shard TTL and one of the in-flight namespaces expired briefly.

kai: So enforcement rejected during the tiny window where the aggregator thought the key had no quota but the batch later showed it did?

maya: Exactly. Reconciliation later fixed customer state but too late for those requests.

ops-sre: Can we add a short "grace window" for enforcer decisions? e.g., if counter < limit + burst_allowance and last-updated < 10s then allow and shadow-log?

jules: I like graceful allowance, but careful: could open up edge for abuse. Maybe a lease-based in-flight increment: acquire short lease per key when request arrives, increment provisional counter, return allowance; reconciliation reconciles lease expiries.

tom: Proposal from my end (quick):
1) Fast-path: keep redis counters but make them authoritative only if last_seen_ts > now - 5s.
2) If last_seen <= 5s or counter TTL expired, enforcer enters "shepherd mode": allow a bounded burst (configurable, default 5 reqs, 2s window) and emit shadow event to pipeline with tag `shepherded=true`.
3) Reconciliation: pipeline marks any shepherded allowances; if batch later shows overage, we create a silent backfill charge and alert billing team, not immediate cutoffs.

maya: +1 but we need operational metrics to notice shepherding rates. Suggest: `metering.shepherd_rate`, `metering.heartbeat_misses`, `metering.enforcer_decisions.shadowed` and a Grafana dashboard.

kai: Also add a consumer-side fix: clients should get informative headers when a request was served under shepherding, e.g. `X-Quota-State: SHEPHERDED;remaining=3;reason=heartbeat-miss`. That helps debugging.

jules: Technical note: implement shepherd leases using the existing redis ring with `SET key lease_id NX EX 3` so we don't block on bigtable. Leases auto-expire.

ops-sre: For alerts, threshold: if shepherd_rate > 0.5% of total requests for more than 1m in a region -> page oncall.

maya: Also want a cleanup path: when pipeline reconciliation finds the counts were actually lower (we allowed too much), we should create a delta record and either refund or apply billing corrections depending on policy. Need finance input.

tom: I'll draft RFC with config knobs: `shepherd.enabled`, `shepherd.burst_limit`, `shepherd.window_s`, `shepherd_shadow_sampling` and an opt-in per-customer toggle for strict enforcement mode.

jules: For rollout: start with `shepherd_shadow_sampling=1.0` for internal orgs, 0.1 for beta customers, monitor `billing.delta` and `safety.events`.

enforcer-bot: Deploy plan created: branch "shepherding-fastpath" -> canary eng-platform-odd -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. CI tests: race/ttl expiry sim, lease contention, batch reconciliation mismatch.

ops-sre: Remember to add integration test that simulates redis shard restart and ensures shepherd mode kicks in without dropping requests.

maya: OK I'm going to open the RFC and link it here. thanks all. :thumbsup:

tom: thanks — also adding a small dashboard mock and the alert rules to the RFC.

jules: FYI I'm documenting the redis key patterns in the RFC (namespace, TTL semantics).

kai: Ping me when it's ready; I'll run chaos test for the heartbeat path.

maya: RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1912345678-shepherding-proposal (draft).

ops-sre: noted. I'll add SLO and paging thresholds in the runbook when RFC lands.

maya: End.
